```{r}
library(data.table)

# Read only the header (no data)
header <- fread("0010290-250426092105405.csv", sep = "\t", nrows = 0)

# Show all column names
names(header)
```

```{r}
library(data.table)
library(arrow)

# Step 1: Specify the GBIF CSV file path
gbif_file <- "0010290-250426092105405.csv"

# Step 2: Define which columns you actually need to extract land cover later
# (Modify this list to include any other fields you care about!)
wanted_cols <- c("decimalLongitude", "decimalLatitude")

# Step 3: Read the header only to check available columns
header <- fread(gbif_file, sep = "\t", nrows = 0)
available_cols <- names(header)

# Check which requested columns actually exist
missing_cols <- setdiff(wanted_cols, available_cols)
if(length(missing_cols) > 0) {
  stop(paste("These columns are missing from the file:", paste(missing_cols, collapse = ", ")))
}

# Step 4: Read *only the columns you need* (very efficient!)
big_csv <- fread(
  gbif_file,
  sep = "\t",
  select = wanted_cols,
  showProgress = TRUE
)

# Step 5: Optional sanity check — peek at first few rows
print(head(big_csv))

# Step 6: Write as Parquet (fast + compressed)
write_parquet(big_csv, "GBIFUS2023.parquet")

cat("✅ Parquet file created: GBIFUS2023.parquet\n")
```
# Convert parquet to SF
```{r}
library(arrow)
library(sf)

# Step 1: Read GBIF data
gbif_data <- read_parquet("GBIFUS2023.parquet")

# Step 2: Remove NAs (do this BEFORE sf conversion to minimize size)
gbif_data <- gbif_data[!is.na(gbif_data$decimalLongitude) & !is.na(gbif_data$decimalLatitude), ]

# Check how many rows (should be ~133 million minus missing coords)
cat("Number of points after removing NAs:", nrow(gbif_data), "\n")

# Step 3: Try sf conversion ONLY
gbif_sf <- st_as_sf(gbif_data, coords = c("decimalLongitude", "decimalLatitude"), crs = 4326)

cat("✅ Successfully converted to sf. Number of points:", nrow(gbif_sf), "\n")
```
